questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence linking two independent clauses:

options.text: The high court dismissed the appeal and the appellant approached the apex court.
The high court dismissed the appeal, and the appellant approached the apex court.
The high court dismissed the appeal, and, approached the apex court.
The high court dismissed the appeal and, the appellant approached the apex court.

questions.explanation: Rule RC-01 ke anusaar, jab coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS) do INDEPENDENT CLAUSES ko connect karta hai ('The high court dismissed the appeal' + 'the appellant approached the apex court'), toh coordinating conjunction ('and') se theek pehle COMMA lagana mandatory hota hai. Option B perfectly accurate hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS) & Clause Comma Rule.
questions.hint: Dono clauses mein subject aur finite verb check karein. Agar dono complete clauses hain, toh 'and' se pehle comma lagna chahiye.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence containing a grammatical error:
"Although the petitioner produced certified copies, (A) / but the revenue officer refused (B) / to mutate the ancestral property (C) / in the official records. (D)"
questions.explanation: Part B mein fatal error hai. Rule RC-02 (Zero Double-Conjunction Law) ke anusaar, jab complex sentence Subordinating Conjunction 'Although' se shuru ho, toh main clause se pehle coordinating conjunction 'but' lagana strictly prohibited hai. Dono clauses ke beech sirf comma aayega. Part B se 'but' ko hatana hoga.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Zero Double-Conjunction Law (Subordinating Trap).
questions.hint: 'Although' sentence ke shuru mein hone par main clause mein 'but' ya 'yet' ki koi zaroorat nahi hoti.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question:
Select the correct sentence to replace the underlined phrase:
"The division bench upheld the conviction, [despite of the material witness turned hostile]."

options.text: despite of the material witness turning hostile
in spite of the material witness turned hostile
although the material witness turned hostile
despite the material witness turned hostile

questions.explanation: 'the material witness turned hostile' ek complete finite clause hai (Subject = 'the material witness', Verb = 'turned'). Finite clause ko introduce karne ke liye subordinating conjunction 'Although' ki zaroorat hoti hai. Prepositions ('despite', 'in spite of') finite clause nahi le sakte, aur 'despite of' English mein exist hi nahi karta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Conjunction vs Preposition: 'Although' vs 'Despite' Rule.
questions.hint: Check karein ki aage finite verb 'turned' hai ya nahi. Finite clause conjunction leta hai, preposition nahi.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.subtopic: Correlative Parallelism: Not only ... but also
questions.question: Choose the sentence that maintains impeccable grammatical parallelism:

options.text: The special tribunal not only granted bail to the applicant but also an unconditional passport return.
The special tribunal granted not only bail to the applicant but also ordered passport return.
The special tribunal granted bail not only to the applicant but also to his co-accused.
Not only the special tribunal granted bail to the applicant but also returned his passport.

questions.explanation: Option C mein 'not only' ke baad prepositional phrase 'to the applicant' hai aur 'but also' ke baad exact matching prepositional phrase 'to his co-accused' hai. Dono arms perfectly parallel hain (Prepositional Phrase + Prepositional Phrase). Option A mein verb 'granted' aur noun phrase 'an unconditional passport return' mismatch hote hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Correlative Conjunctions & Strict Structural Parallelism.
questions.hint: 'Not only' aur 'but also' dono ke theek baad aane wale words ka grammatical form exact same hona chahiye.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb form:
"Neither the public prosecutor nor the defense advocates ________ willing to concede on the bail conditions."
questions.explanation: Rule RC-05 ke anusaar, jab 'Neither...nor' do subjects ko connect karta hai, toh main verb NEAREST subject ke hisab se agree karti hai. Blank ke theek pehle Subject 2 'the defense advocates' (Plural) hai, isliye past tense plural verb 'were' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Proximity Agreement with Correlative Subjects.
questions.hint: 'Nor' ke theek baad aane wale subject ko dekhein. Agar wo plural hai, toh verb bhi plural lagegi.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question:
Identify the error in the sentence:
"Hardly had the arbitrator (A) / commenced the hearing (B) / than an urgent objection (C) / was raised by the respondent. (D)"
questions.explanation: Part C mein error hai. Rule RC-06 ke anusaar, 'Hardly', 'Scarcely', aur 'Barely' ke sath correlative partner strictly 'WHEN' hota hai, 'THAN' lagana fatal error hai. Part C mein 'than' ko replace karke 'when' likhna hoga: 'when an urgent objection was raised'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Inversion with 'Hardly / Scarcely / Barely ... WHEN'.
questions.hint: 'Hardly' ke sath 'than' kabhi nahi lagta. 'Than' sirf 'No sooner' ke sath aata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically sound?

options.text: No sooner had the registry received the summons when the process server was dispatched.
No sooner did the registry received the summons than the process server was dispatched.
No sooner had the registry received the summons than the process server was dispatched.
No sooner had the registry received the summons then the process server was dispatched.

questions.explanation: Option C perfectly accurate hai. 'No sooner had + Subject + V3' valid auxiliary inversion follow karta hai aur comparative connective partner 'THAN' (spelled with 'A') se match karta hai. Option A mein 'when' galat hai, Option B mein 'did' ke sath V2 'received' lagaya gaya hai jo ungrammatical hai ('did' ke sath base form 'receive' aani chahiye), aur Option D mein 'then' galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Inversion with 'No Sooner ... THAN'.
questions.hint: 'No sooner' ke sath 'than' dekhein (spelled t-h-a-n, not t-h-e-n).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the grammatically correct clause:
"Deposit the certified court fees today, lest your application ________."
questions.explanation: Rule RC-08 ke anusaar, 'lest' (taaki aisa na ho) ke sath modal auxiliary strictly 'SHOULD' aati hai aur iske clause ke andar 'NOT' lagana strictly prohibited hota hai (double negative error). Isliye Option C 'should be rejected' sahi answer hai.
questions.hint: 'Lest' khud negative hota hai, isliye iske baad doosra negative word 'not' nahi lag sakta.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct words:
"The high court ruling will profoundly ________ pending arbitration cases, producing an immediate ________ on corporate settlements."
questions.explanation: Pehle blank mein modal 'will' ke baad base form of VERB chahiye: 'affect' (to influence). Doosre blank mein article 'an' aur adjective 'immediate' ke baad NOUN chahiye: 'effect' (the result/impact). Isliye Option B 'affect, effect' sahi answer hai.
questions.hint: Remember RAVEN: Affect is Verb, Effect is Noun.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill the blanks:
"The ________ ground of appeal was that the trial court violated the legal ________ of audi alteram partem."
questions.explanation: Pehle blank mein noun 'ground' ko qualify karne ke liye Adjective 'Principal' (meaning: main / primary) chahiye: 'The principal ground'. Doosre blank mein legal doctrine / kanooni niyam ki baat ho rahi hai, jiske liye Noun 'Principle' (meaning: moral rule/doctrine) chahiye. Option B sahi hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-12: Confused Words: 'Principal' (Main/Head) vs 'Principle' (Moral Rule).
questions.hint: PrinciPLE ends in -LE like ruLE. PrinciPAL means main or chief officer.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence:
"The scientific laboratory report ________ the circumstantial evidence, thereby sealing the conviction."
questions.explanation: 'Complement' (with 'e') ka arth hota hai kisi doosri cheez ko poora karna ya uske sath judkar use complete banana ('poorak banna'). Scientific report ne circumstantial evidence ko complete kiya, uski tareef nahi ki. Past tense context mein 'complemented' (Option B) correct hai. 'Complimented' (with 'i') tareef karne ke liye use hota hai.
questions.hint: ComplEment has an 'E' for complEte. ComplIment has an 'I' for prAIse.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct verb form:
"Yesterday morning, the senior advocate ________ the complete trial brief before the bench for scrutiny."
questions.explanation: Sentence mein verb ke baad DIRECT OBJECT 'the complete trial brief' maujood hai ('Whom/What did he lay? ➔ The trial brief'). Kisi cheez ko rakhne ke liye Transitive verb 'LAY' use hoti hai jiska Simple Past tense 'LAID' hota hai. Isliye Option B sahi hai. 'Lay' intransitive 'lie' ka past hota hai jiske baad direct object nahi lag sakta.
questions.hint: Check karein: verb ke baad direct object 'the trial brief' hai. Object hone par 'lay/laid' use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L15
